summary.intent: The user was frustrated with the quality of changeset text in recent PRs and wanted it cleaned up, as part of building a system for better changesets. They want entries that are mindful, plain, and written as release notes rather than implementation notes.
summary.outcome: Deleted the unnecessary changeset on PR #485 because the finding it fixes is new in 0.19.0 and unreleased. Rewrote #483's changeset twice, first as one plain sentence and then to say why the PR link helps. Started a new worktree/branch (docs/changeset-set) off origin/main for the broader changeset work, which is not yet done.

repo: Changesets live in .changeset/ and are checked in per PR. The repo has an AGENTS.md and .changeset/README.md with changeset guidance, which the assistant consulted mid-session.
Commits are GPG/SSH signed (git commit -S) and pushed straight to the PR branch.
The 0.19.0 changelog had 13 entries, most of them fix-ups to features not yet shipped, so they should not get their own changesets.
Work is done in git worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ (e.g. change-pr-links, changeset-set).
workflow: A fix to a feature that has not been released needs no changeset, because users never saw the broken behavior.
Changeset text should be written for users as release notes: short, plain, no backstory or implementation detail, and should say why a change helps.
The assistant's own memory notes already said to keep changesets short and plain, but it did not follow them, so the guidance needs to be checked before writing entries.
The assistant read AGENTS.md and the changeset README only after its first rewrite, and the second rewrite was needed as a result; reading the conventions first would have saved a commit.

friction: The assistant wrote careless changesets that explained implementation and read like debugging notes, which caused the user's frustration.
The first rewrite of the #483 changeset was incomplete and needed a second commit to say why the link helps, not just what it does.
Many changesets for the 0.19.0 release were over-granular, covering fix-ups to unreleased features.
open_items: Review and fix the remaining changesets in the 0.19.0 set, which was started in the docs/changeset-set worktree.
Consolidate the 13 entries in the 0.19.0 changelog down to ones users actually need.
Build the system for better changesets that the user mentioned, which is still in progress.
